title: Fish and Rice with Cream Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Fish and rice with cream sauce is a dish that combines tender white fish, fluffy rice, and a smooth cream‑based sauce. Commonly used fish includes cod, haddock, or pollock, and the sauce is made from cream, butter, and a blend of herbs and spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cream sauce often includes a splash of lemon juice to brighten the flavor of the fish.
The dish is popular in both European and Asian cuisines, where rice serves as a staple side.
Omega‑3 rich fish enhances the aromatic profile of the cream sauce.
It is traditionally served hot, but can also be baked in a casserole dish for a one‑pan meal.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Fish provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: EPA and DHA support cardiovascular health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fish is a good source of B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are important for metabolism and nerve function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish supplies selenium, iodine, and phosphorus, beneficial for thyroid function and bone health.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides steady‑release energy, helping to keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including fish.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: The cream sauce adds saturated fat; people monitoring cholesterol should watch portion size.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improperly stored fish can harbor bacteria or parasites; always observe proper refrigeration and cooking times.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Cream and prepared sauces often contain salt; those with hypertension should limit added salt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, mixing fish, rice, and sauce on a plate. Garnish with fresh herbs (parsley, dill) or lemon wedges for extra brightness. It pairs well with steamed vegetables or a green salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. When reheating, add a splash of cream or broth to prevent the sauce from drying out. For longer storage, freeze fish and rice separately; the cream sauce does not freeze well.
